message.content:
Driving from San Francisco to Los Angeles is roughly 380–400 miles (about 610–640 km) depending on the exact route you take. On a clear day, with no major stops and staying within speed limits, you can expect the trip to take around **6 to 7 hours**.  

If you’re heading out during rush hour or on a weekend when traffic can be heavy, add an extra hour or two. And remember that the actual time can vary with weather, construction, and how many breaks you take along the way.

We can provide approximate driving distance (~383 miles via I-5) and typical driving time (~6 hours). But we might also mention traffic, speed limits, etc. There's no need to call the function.
